canvas-01.description: Sheet 1 covers the west side of Milford between the Delaware River and the foot of the steep slope above the town, from the north end of Spring Garden Street down to Bridge Street. Along the river run the Pennsylvania Railroad (Belvidere Division) and Railroad Avenue, with a footpath on the driveway beside the tracks. Spring Garden Street runs parallel to them up the sheet, lined with dwellings (numbers 201 to 235 and 301 to 322), hen houses, sheds and a bicycle repair shop. Church Street crosses the sheet below them; the Christian Church, heated by steam with a 90 ft spire, stands on its north side in front of a cemetery on the slope. Church Street Square runs from Church Street down to Bridge Street, which forms the bottom edge of the sheet. The block between Railroad Avenue and Church Street Square holds a pump house, dwellings and, along Bridge Street, the commercial row with a barber, the post office, a drug store and stores; east of the square are the Gibson House hotel and bar, a large hotel building, and further shops and dwellings along Bridge Street towards the iron bridge over the creek, reached by a curving Drive, a Lane and a Driveway. At the lower left the covered wooden bridge to Pennsylvania, 677 ft long, leaves Bridge Street across the river. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch, turned so that north points to the upper right. The key map of the town, the index of specials, notes on water facilities and the fire department and the legend are printed on the sheet and are not part of the map area.
notes: Church Street Square is today part of Church Street, which runs from Bridge Street north and then turns west to Spring Garden Street as on the sheet.
Race Street is Carpenter Street today.
Spring Garden Street north of Church Street has been realigned: the modern street crosses the 1912 lots, so only its junction with Church Street was used.
The north half of the sheet has no control point; it is placed by extrapolation from three points near Church and Bridge streets.

Printed sheet 1, January 1912. Spring Garden Street, Railroad Avenue, Church Street, Church Street Square, Bridge Street, Drive, Lane; Delaware River and Pennsylvania shore. Key map, index of specials, water facilities and legend printed top right and lower left: masked out. Scale 50 ft to an inch. Spring Garden Street north of Church Street has been realigned since (the modern way crosses the 1912 lots), so only its junction with Church Street is used.

canvas-05-1.description: The main part of sheet 3 covers the low ground of Milford between the Delaware River and Quequacommissicong Creek, south of Bridge Street. Bridge Street runs along the top of the sheet from the covered wooden bridge to Pennsylvania (567 ft long, drawn at the upper left) east to the iron bridge over the creek; its south side is the town's business row, with the First National Bank, general stores, a photographer, a building with a harrow shop on the ground floor and the O. F. Hall on the third, a printing office and a tin shop. Below these lots the Head Race of the Thomas mill crosses the blocks to the river. Railroad Avenue runs down the sheet beside the Pennsylvania Railroad (Belvidere Division), whose main line, sidings and long passing siding fill the strip along the river with the passenger depot, freight house, coal sheds, a hand car and tool house, a water tank and a steam pump. Between the tracks and the river stand the W. & W. E. Thomas Milford flour mill, with its storehouse, penstock and machinery notes, and further south the Henry Hauptfuhrer creamery near the cattle pens. East of Railroad Avenue are residential blocks along Green, Maple and Orchard streets, bounded on the east by Race Street, with J. C. Stem's chair factory at Green Street and the Opera House across Race Street. The east margin is open ground along the winding creek. The sheet is drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right; the public school is shown in a separate inset at the lower left.
notes: Race Street is Carpenter Street today; Green, Maple and Orchard are Green Street, Maple Street and Orchard Street.
Only the east side of Railroad Avenue is drawn (the west side is railroad land); its four junctions were hand-picked 12 ft west of the drawn east edge, half the modern right-of-way.
The Pennsylvania Railroad (Belvidere Division) through Milford is abandoned; the former line is not in the modern railroad data.

Printed sheet 3, January 1912. Bridge Street, Railroad Avenue, Green, Maple, Orchard, Race Street; Pennsylvania Railroad (Belvidere Division), W. & W. E. Thomas Milford Mill, covered bridge to Pennsylvania. Inset lower left: Public School on Mt. Pleasant Road and Frenchtown Road. Scale 50 ft to an inch.

canvas-05-2.description: A small inset in the lower left corner of sheet 3, separated from the main map by a heavy line, shows the Milford public school on open ground east of town where Mt. Pleasant Road leaves French Town Road. The only building drawn is the school itself, a two-storey stone building with notes that it has no lights and is heated by steam, and a note giving 185 ft to the fire department. French Town Road crosses the lower left corner and Mt. Pleasant Road curves away from it along the bottom of the inset; the scale bar of the sheet (50 ft to an inch) is printed inside the inset. The inset has its own north arrow, drawn at about the same angle as the arrow of the main map, and is drawn at the same scale. The rest of the inset is blank, bounded on the right by a line marked no exposure.
notes: French Town Road is Frenchtown Road today; Mt. Pleasant Road is Milford - Mount Pleasant Road in OpenStreetMap.
Placed from one hand-picked point, the meeting of the two roads at the corner of the inset, with the scale and rotation of the main part of the sheet: low confidence.

Printed sheet 3, January 1912. Bridge Street, Railroad Avenue, Green, Maple, Orchard, Race Street; Pennsylvania Railroad (Belvidere Division), W. & W. E. Thomas Milford Mill, covered bridge to Pennsylvania. Inset lower left: Public School on Mt. Pleasant Road and Frenchtown Road. Scale 50 ft to an inch.

sheet-2-1.description: The right-hand part of sheet 2, separated from the left by a heavy line, covers the north end of Milford along Water Street and Mill Street on both sides of the Quequacommissicong Creek. At the top the W. & W. E. Thomas feed and grist mill stands between the Head Race and the creek, with its office, wagon shed, a corn crib and machinery notes (a 30 horsepower water wheel and a pump supplying water to the town reservoir). York Street leaves Water Street towards the northeast, meets Mill Street at a fork and continues to the top right corner of the sheet as a row of houses numbered 101 to 120 on both sides. Mill Street runs south from the fork, crosses the creek on an iron bridge and continues to the bottom of the sheet; Water Street crosses the creek on its own iron bridge further west. Private Street joins Water and Mill streets south of the creek, and the block below it is lined with dwellings along Water Street (numbers 319 to 361) and Mill Street. The Head Race runs from the top of the sheet past a wooden bridge to the mill. The part is drawn at 50 ft to an inch with north towards the top, at a different angle from the left part of the sheet, and the margins to the east are marked no exposure.
notes: York (northeast of Mill Street) is York Road today; the short stretch between Water and Mill streets is York Street.
Private Street does not survive as a street in OpenStreetMap.

Placed from three points: the detected junction of Mill Street, York Street and York Road, the hand-picked Water Street / York Street junction, and a hydrant on Water Street drawn on both parts of the sheet (carried from part 2): an exact fit with no check on its error, and a scale about 5 percent below the other sheets: low confidence.

Printed sheet 2, January 1912. Water Street, Mill Street, Quequa, Bridge Street, Frenchtown Road, Lane, York Street, Private Street; Quequacommissicong Creek, Head Race, W. & W. E. Thomas feed and grist mill. Scale 50 ft to an inch.

sheet-2-2.description: The left-hand part of sheet 2 covers the centre of Milford along Water Street, from Bridge Street at the bottom to Quequa Street at the top, between the Quequacommissicong Creek on the west and Mill Street on the east. Water Street is lined with houses, stores and outbuildings (numbers 301 to 318 on the west side, 335 to 353 on the east), among them the Milford House hotel and bar, the old horse sheds, a pool room, an ice house, a slaughter house with a steam engine, the Samuel Raub carriage shop and wheelwright, a cobbler and a band hall. A narrow triangular green separates Water Street from Mill Street, which leaves Water Street towards the north; the Methodist church, no longer used, stands at the corner below it. At the bottom Bridge Street crosses the creek on an iron bridge, with a dam just south of it, and the Presbyterian church with its church sheds and the fire department engine house stand west of Water Street. Frenchtown Road runs southeast from the junction past a lane, the vacant buildings of the former Central Lumber and Manufacturing Company and the former E. C. Hurley creamery. The part is drawn at 50 ft to an inch, turned so that north points up and slightly to the right, and is cut by a heavy line from the right-hand part of the sheet.
notes: Quequa Street is Pine Street today.
Mill Street meets Water Street at a long, sharp fork, so that junction was not used.
Placed from three points (two detected on Quequa Street, one hand-picked at Bridge Street): an exact fit with no check on its error.

Printed sheet 2, January 1912. Water Street, Mill Street, Quequa, Bridge Street, Frenchtown Road, Lane, York Street, Private Street; Quequacommissicong Creek, Head Race, W. & W. E. Thomas feed and grist mill. Scale 50 ft to an inch.
